subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — plugin emission API and manifest policy

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this six-event AI-safety taxonomy and a permanent manifest-gated plugin emission contract, despite plugins already being trusted in-process code?
rationale: The choice defines public plugin SDK, manifest, telemetry-integrity, privacy, and versioning contracts; correctness repairs cannot decide whether that permanent product surface should exist or what its trust semantics should be.

options.title: Sponsor a host-bound redesign
options.body: Approve the capability direction but require host-derived plugin identity, normalized manifest declarations, complete runtime validation, canonical session context, and installed-plugin proof before merge.

options.title: Keep diagnostics internal
options.body: Retain safety events as core-owned diagnostics and have plugins contribute through existing typed hooks without a new manifest permission or public emission API.

options.title: Pause the taxonomy series
options.body: Leave the canonical issue open for design evidence and close or replace the stacked implementation PRs if maintainers do not want to own this contract now.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a host-bound redesign
recommendation.body: Approve the capability direction but require host-derived plugin identity, normalized manifest declarations, complete runtime validation, canonical session context, and installed-plugin proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to plugin manifest policy and product/security review of new plugin contracts.
